# DocuSign v3.5.1 - Table of Contents

> Unofficial DocuSign Elixir Library used to interact with the eSign REST API.

## GUIDES

- [README](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/readme.md)

- Guides
  - [DocuSign Embedded Signing with Elixir](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/embedded_signing.md)
  - [DocuSign OAuth2 Authorization Code Flow with Elixir](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/oauth_authorization_code_flow.md)

- Migration Guides
  - [Migration Guide](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/migrating.md)

- Changelog
  - [Changelog](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/changelog.md)

## Modules

- [DocuSign](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.md): Documentation for DocuSign Elixir SDK.

- [DocuSign.Debug](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Debug.md): Debugging and logging configuration for the DocuSign Elixir client.
- [DocuSign.Deserializer](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Deserializer.md): Helper functions for deserializing responses into models

- [DocuSign.FileDownloader](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.FileDownloader.md): File download utilities for DocuSign documents and attachments.
- [DocuSign.RequestBuilder](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.RequestBuilder.md): Helper functions for building Req requests

- [DocuSign.SDKVersion](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.SDKVersion.md): SDK version information and User-Agent header management.
- [DocuSign.SSLOptions](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.SSLOptions.md): Provides SSL configuration options for DocuSign API connections.
- [DocuSign.Telemetry](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Telemetry.md): Telemetry integration for DocuSign API operations.

- Models
  - [DocuSign.Model.AccessCodeFormat](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.AccessCodeFormat.md): Object specifying the format of the string provided to a recipient in order to access an envelope.

  - [DocuSign.Model.AccountAddress](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.AccountAddress.md): Contains information about the address associated with the account.

  - [DocuSign.Model.AccountBillingPlan](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.AccountBillingPlan.md): Contains information about an account billing plan.

  - [DocuSign.Model.AccountBillingPlanResponse](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.AccountBillingPlanResponse.md): Defines an account billing plan response object.

  - [DocuSign.Model.AccountBrands](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.AccountBrands.md): The AccountBrands resource enables you to use account-level brands to customize the styles and text that recipients see.

  - [DocuSign.Model.AccountConsumerDisclosures](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.AccountConsumerDisclosures.md): Details about account consumer disclosures.

  - [DocuSign.Model.AccountCustomFields](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.AccountCustomFields.md): An `accountCustomField` is an envelope custom field that you set at the account level. Applying custom fields enables account administrators to group and manage envelopes.

  - [DocuSign.Model.AccountPasswordRules](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.AccountPasswordRules.md): Contains details about the password rules for an account.

  - [DocuSign.Model.BccEmailArchive](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.BccEmailArchive.md): The `EmailArchive` resource provides methods for managing your email archive configuration, which consists of the BCC email address or addresses that you want to use to archive Docusign emails. Each account can use up to five BCC email addresses for archiving purposes. 

  - [DocuSign.Model.BccEmailArchiveHistory](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.BccEmailArchiveHistory.md): Contains details about the history of the BCC email archive configuration.

To match up, the `tabLabel` for this tab and the `tabLabel` for the corresponding tab on the envelope or template must be the same.  For example, if the envelope has a placeholder text tab with the `tabLabel` `childName`, you must assign the same `tabLabel` `childName` to the tab here that you are populating with that information.

The format entered by the signer is retained. If you need a particular date format enforced, Docusign recommends using a Text tab with a validation pattern and a validation message to enforce the format.

This parameter uses pixel positioning to draw a rectangle at the center of the stamp area. The stamp is superimposed on top of this central area.  This property contains the following information about the central rectangle:  - `DateAreaX`: The X axis position of the top-left corner. - `DateAreaY`: The Y axis position of the top-left corner. - `DateAreaWidth`: The width of the rectangle. - `DateAreaHeight`: The height of the rectangle.

  - [DocuSign.Model.Editor](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.Editor.md): A complex type defining the management and access rights of a recipient assigned as an editor on the envelope. Editors have the same management and access rights for the envelope as the sender. They can make changes to the envelope as if they were using the Correct feature. This recipient can add name and email information, add or change the routing order and set authentication options for the remaining recipients. Additionally, this recipient can edit signature/initial tabs and text tabs for the remaining recipients.

  - [DocuSign.Model.Email](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.Email.md): A tab that allows the recipient to enter an email address. This is a one-line field that checks that a valid email address is entered. It uses the same parameters as a Text tab, with the validation message and pattern set for email information.  When getting information that includes this tab type, the original value of the tab when the associated envelope was sent is included in the response. 

  - [DocuSign.Model.EmailAddress](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.EmailAddress.md): A tab that displays the recipient's email as entered in the recipient information. 

  - [DocuSign.Model.EmailSettings](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.EmailSettings.md): A complex element that allows  the sender to override some envelope email setting information. This can be used to override the Reply To email address and name associated with the envelope and to override the BCC email addresses to which an envelope is sent.   When the emailSettings information is used for an envelope, it only applies to that envelope.   **IMPORTANT:** The emailSettings information is not returned in the GET for envelope status. Use GET /email_settings to return information about the emailSettings.   EmailSettings consists of:   * replyEmailAddressOverride - The Reply To email used for the envelope. Docusign will verify that a correct email format is used, but does not verify that the email is active. Maximum Length: 100 characters. * replyEmailNameOverride - The name associated with the Reply To email address. Maximum Length: 100 characters. * bccEmailAddresses - An array of up to five email addresses to which the envelope is sent to as a BCC email. Only users with canManageAccount setting set to true can use this option.  Docusign verifies that the email format is correct, but does not verify that the email is active. Using this overrides the BCC for Email Archive information setting for this envelope. Maximum Length: 100 characters. *Example*: if your account has BCC for Email Archive set up for the email address 'archive@mycompany.com' and you send an envelope using the BCC Email Override to send a BCC email to 'salesarchive@mycompany.com', then a copy of the envelope is only sent to the 'salesarchive@mycompany.com' email address.

You can then use the custom data for sorting, organizing, searching, and other downstream processes. For example, you can use custom fields to copy envelopes or data to multiple areas in Salesforce. eOriginal customers can eVault their documents from the web app on a per-envelope basis by setting an envelope custom field with a name like "eVault with eOriginal?" to "Yes" or "No".  When a user creates an envelope, the envelope custom fields display in the **Envelope Settings** section of the Docusign console. Envelope recipients do not see the envelope custom fields. For more information, see [Envelope Custom Fields](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?bundleId=pik1583277475390&topicId=qor1583277385137.html).

  - [DocuSign.Model.EnvelopeDocumentVisibility](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.EnvelopeDocumentVisibility.md): Document Visibility enables senders to control the visibility of the documents in an envelope at the recipient level. For example, if the parties associated with a legal proceeding should have access to different documents, the Document Visibility feature enables you to keep all of the documents in the same envelope and set view permissions for the documents by recipient. This functionality is enabled for envelopes and templates. It is not available for PowerForms.  **Note:** Before you use Document Visibility, you should be aware of the following information:  - Document Visibility must be enabled for your account by your Docusign administrator.  - A document cannot be hidden from a recipient if the recipient has tabs assigned to them on the document.  - When the Document Visibility setting hides a document from a recipient, the document also does not appear in the recipient's list of envelopes, documents, or page images. - Carbon Copy, Certified Delivery (Needs to Sign), Editor, and Agent recipients can always see all of the documents associated with the envelope or template.  The Document Visibility feature has multiple settings that specify the options that senders have when sending documents. For more information, see [Use Document Visibility to Control Recipient Access](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?bundleId=gbo1643332197980&topicId=eui1578456411411.html).

  - [DocuSign.Model.SealSign](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.SealSign.md): Specifies one or more electronic seals to apply on documents. An electronic seal recipient is a legal entity rather than an actual person. Electronic Seals can be used by organizations and governments to show evidence of origin and integrity of documents. Even though electronic seals can be represented by a tab in a document, they do not require user interaction and apply automatically in the order specified by the sender. The sender is therefore the person authorizing usage of the electronic seal in the flow.  Example:  ```json "recipients": {       "seals": [         {           "recipientId": "1",           "routingOrder" : 1,           "recipientSignatureProviders": [             {               "sealName": "52e9d968-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-4682bc45c106"             }         ]       }     ]   },     .     .     . ``` For more information about Electronic Seals, see [Apply Electronic Seals to Your Documents](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?bundleId=xcm1643837555908&topicId=isl1578456577247.html).

Signing groups enable you to send an envelope to a predefined group of recipients and have any one member of the group sign your documents. When you send an envelope to a signing group, anyone in the group can open it and sign it with their own signature.

  - [DocuSign.Model.TemplateDocumentVisibility](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.TemplateDocumentVisibility.md): Document Visibility enables senders to control the visibility of the documents in an envelope at the recipient level. For example, if the parties associated with a legal proceeding should have access to different documents, the Document Visibility feature enables you to keep all of the documents in the same envelope and set view permissions for the documents by recipient. This functionality is enabled for envelopes and templates. It is not available for PowerForms.  **Note:** Before you use Document Visibility, you should be aware of the following information:  - Document Visibility must be enabled for your account by your Docusign administrator.  - A document cannot be hidden from a recipient if the recipient has tabs assigned to them on the document.  - When the Document Visibility setting hides a document from a recipient, the document also does not appear in the recipient's list of envelopes, documents, or page images. - Carbon Copy, Certified Delivery (Needs to Sign), Editor, and Agent recipients can always see all of the documents associated with the envelope or template.  The Document Visibility feature has multiple settings that specify the options that senders have when sending documents. For more information, see [Use Document Visibility to Control Recipient Access](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?bundleId=gbo1643332197980&topicId=eui1578456411411.html).

  - [DocuSign.Model.TemplateDocumentVisibilityList](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Model.TemplateDocumentVisibilityList.md): A list of `documentVisibility` objects that specify whether the documents associated with a template are visible to recipients.

The zip code can be typed with or without dashes. It uses the same parameters as a Text tab, with the validation message and pattern set for ZIP code information. 

- Core
  - [DocuSign.ClientRegistry](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.ClientRegistry.md): GenServer to store API clients and automatically refresh JWT access tokens.
  - [DocuSign.Connection](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Connection.md): The module is intended to be used to establish a connection with
DocuSign eSignature API and then perform requests to it.
  - [DocuSign.ConnectionPool](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.ConnectionPool.md): Connection pooling configuration for high-throughput DocuSign applications.
  - [DocuSign.OAuth](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.OAuth.md): This module defines the behaviour of the OAuth adapter.

  - [DocuSign.OAuth.AuthorizationCodeStrategy](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.OAuth.AuthorizationCodeStrategy.md): OAuth2 Authorization Code Flow strategy for DocuSign using the battle-tested oauth2 library.
  - [DocuSign.OAuth.Fake](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.OAuth.Fake.md): Fake OAuth implementation mainly for test environment.

  - [DocuSign.OAuth.Impl](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.OAuth.Impl.md): This module implements the OAuth behaviour and an oauth2 strategy for DocuSign.
  - [DocuSign.User](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.User.md): This module contains the User struct and functions for working with it.
  - [DocuSign.Util.Environment](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Util.Environment.md): Utilities for automatic environment detection based on DocuSign URLs.

- WebHook
  - [DocuSign.Webhook.Crypto](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Webhook.Crypto.md): Crypto functions for DocuSign HMAC signature validation.

  - [DocuSign.Webhook.Handler](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Webhook.Handler.md): Webhook handler behaviour.

  - [DocuSign.WebhookPlug](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.WebhookPlug.md): Helper `Plug` to process webhook events and send them to a custom handler.

- Exceptions
  - [DocuSign.ApiError](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.ApiError.md): Generic API error.

  - [DocuSign.AuthenticationError](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.AuthenticationError.md): Authentication error (401).

  - [DocuSign.Error](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.Error.md): Defines structured errors for the DocuSign API client.

  - [DocuSign.NetworkError](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.NetworkError.md): Network-related error.

  - [DocuSign.RateLimitError](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.RateLimitError.md): Rate limit exceeded error (429).

  - [DocuSign.ValidationError](https://docusign.hexdocs.pm/DocuSign.ValidationError.md): Validation error (400).
